findings.title: Floor division replaces ceiling division, silently dropping the last partial page
findings.explanation: The original expression `(total + size - 1) // size` is the standard ceiling-division idiom: it returns the number of pages required to hold `total` items at `size` items per page, rounding up so that any remainder produces an additional page. The replacement `total // size` performs floor division, which truncates the remainder. Whenever `total` is not an exact multiple of `size`, the function now returns one fewer page than needed, silently discarding the last partial page of items. For example, `pages(10, 3)` previously returned 4 (pages of 3,3,3,1) but now returns 3, losing the final item. This is a logic regression that will cause data loss in any caller that relies on the page count to iterate over or display all items.
findings.suggestion: Revert to the ceiling-division formula: `return (total + size - 1) // size`, or equivalently use `import math; return math.ceil(total / size)` if floating-point semantics are acceptable. If the intent was genuinely to floor, the function name `pages` is misleading and callers must be audited.
findings.trigger_condition: total % size != 0 (i.e., total is not evenly divisible by size)
